new_findings_today.title: robots.txt advertises a 6th sitemap chunk (/sitemap/5.xml — Q&A) that returns HTTP 404 and is absent from the sitemap index
new_findings_today.detail: robots.txt lists six `Sitemap:` directives (/sitemap/0.xml through /sitemap/5.xml) and its comment documents the intended split as '6 chunks: static, destinations, content, programmatic SEO, comparisons, Q&A'. But the sitemap index at /sitemap.xml lists only 5 chunks (0.xml-4.xml), and a direct probe of /sitemap/5.xml returns HTTP 404 with a 9-byte 'Not Found' body. So the Q&A sitemap chunk is advertised to crawlers but does not exist. This is a latent inconsistency, NOT a regression introduced by today's deploy: robots.txt is byte-identical across runs (1879 bytes on both 2026-05-22 and 2026-05-23), and the sitemap index also listed only 5 chunks on 2026-05-22 — the mismatch predates this run and was simply not cross-checked before. Section H of the daily matrix only validates chunks referenced BY the index (all 5 of which load and are well-formed), so the robots.txt-vs-index discrepancy slipped past prior passes. Impact is bounded: search engines and AI-answer bots that read robots.txt Sitemap directives will fetch /sitemap/5.xml, get a 404, and skip it gracefully; Q&A URLs (if a Q&A surface exists) would not gain sitemap-driven discovery, but they may still be crawled via on-site links. No user-facing breakage.
new_findings_today.evidence: section-J probe block: robots.txt body shows 6 `Sitemap:` lines + the '6 chunks ... Q&A' comment; sitemap-index.xml shows 5 <loc> entries (0-4); curl https://www.nakshiq.com/sitemap/5.xml -> HTTP 404, 9-byte body, not XML. robots.txt unchanged at 1879 bytes vs 2026-05-22 http-matrix.csv.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Reconcile robots.txt with the sitemap generator: either (a) generate and deploy /sitemap/5.xml (the Q&A chunk) so it matches the advertised 6-chunk layout and add it to the sitemap index, or (b) if the Q&A surface was folded into another chunk or dropped, remove the 6th `Sitemap:` line and correct the '6 chunks' comment in robots.txt. Low severity / SEO hygiene — schedule alongside the next SEO sweep, not urgent.
